title: I had Claude draw my game's town. It can't really draw, which is fun
author: No_End_3558
selftext:
My browser trading game showed a plain menu between trading days. I wanted a place instead: buildings, a clock, a doorman deciding who gets into the bar. The street got drawn with Claude . No "image generation" anywhere.

The sprites are text. Every one is a string-array grid in the game file, one character per pixel. It reads and writes a sprite the way it reads and writes code. Which means it can't really draw, and that's the fun part.   
  
You build the picture together: where the floor line is, what a chair back has to touch, why a five-wide awning can't center on a six-wide door. It fails the way a person fails confidently and gets better the same way.

Every composition was dumped back to ASCII and machine-checked before I looked, and a hard rule to regenerate the whole sprite from its description rather than patch pixels in place.

The art is crude but is starting to have a vibe. Instead of a menu its a seedy alley.
